{
  "summary": "Encapsulates CTransaction data members behind public const observer functions (such as GetInputs() and GetOutputs()) and makes the underlying member variables private and non-const. Direct member accesses across the codebase are mechanically migrated to the observers using a newly added bitcoin-tidy check. Matching observer member functions are also added to CMutableTransaction to facilitate generic code.",
  "problem": "CTransaction exposes its data members directly as public const variables to enforce immutability. This locks the internal representation into the public API, prevents the class from modeling a regular value type with copy and move assignment, and blocks cleanly separating serialization and validation functionality from the type.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: \"Once access goes through observers, the representation can change without requiring its users to change as well. This establishes a clean boundary between the transaction's data and functionality that operates on it. In particular, it allows serialization/deserialization and other functionality to be separated from the type itself in subsequent refactorings.\"",
    "PR description: \"This work is part of the broader interface-segregation direction described in #35904, but is not a prerequisite for the stateless validation library proposed there. The encapsulation has value independently of that work.\""
  ],
  "dependencies": {

    ]
  },
  "scope_notes": "Most of the diff is a mechanical search-and-replace across 94 files generated by a custom clang-tidy check introduced in the branch (bitcoin-use-observers).",
  "changed_since_previous": "Added a commit replacing decltype(CTransaction::version) with explicit uint32_t types in policy and RPC code, necessitated by making CTransaction's version member private.",
  "card": "Encapsulates CTransaction data members behind public observer methods, migrating direct member accesses across the codebase and making the underlying members private and non-const. Today, CTransaction exposes public const members to guarantee immutability, which locks the representation into the public API and prevents regular value semantics like assignment. Decoupling callers from internal storage layout facilitates future refactorings to separate serialization and stateless validation logic as outlined in issue #35904. result.summary: Encapsulates CTransaction data members behind public const observer functions (such as GetInputs() and GetOutputs()) and makes the underlying member variables private and non-const. Direct member accesses across the codebase are mechanically migrated to the observers using a newly added bitcoin-tidy check. Matching observer member functions are also added to CMutableTransaction to facilitate generic code.
result.problem: CTransaction exposes its data members directly as public const variables to enforce immutability. This locks the internal representation into the public API, prevents the class from modeling a regular value type with copy and move assignment, and blocks cleanly separating serialization and validation functionality from the type.
evidence: PR description: "Once access goes through observers, the representation can change without requiring its users to change as well. This establishes a clean boundary between the transaction's data and functionality that operates on it. In particular, it allows serialization/deserialization and other functionality to be separated from the type itself in subsequent refactorings."

PR description: "This work is part of the broader interface-segregation direction described in #35904, but is not a prerequisite for the stateless validation library proposed there. The encapsulation has value independently of that work."
result.scope_notes: Most of the diff is a mechanical search-and-replace across 94 files generated by a custom clang-tidy check introduced in the branch (bitcoin-use-observers).
result.changed_since_previous: Added a commit replacing decltype(CTransaction::version) with explicit uint32_t types in policy and RPC code, necessitated by making CTransaction's version member private.
result.card: Encapsulates CTransaction data members behind public observer methods, migrating direct member accesses across the codebase and making the underlying members private and non-const. Today, CTransaction exposes public const members to guarantee immutability, which locks the representation into the public API and prevents regular value semantics like assignment. Decoupling callers from internal storage layout facilitates future refactorings to separate serialization and stateless validation logic as outlined in issue #35904. Most of the 94 files modified are updated mechanically via a custom clang-tidy check introduced in the branch.

risk.why: A typo or incorrect observer implementation across this widespread refactor could alter validation checks or transaction serialization, causing node desyncs or transaction signing errors.
